modules.summary: Models hallmark 1 as oncogenic lesion -> constitutive RAS-MAPK/PI3K flux -> growth-factor-independent proliferation, with a therapeutic-vulnerability node (oncogene addiction) and an adaptive-escape node (ERK signal persistence). The chain is valid and the two therapeutic nodes are a genuine addition rather than a drug monograph: both carry their own primary-literature evidence and the description tells a conforming entry what to put on each. It is the most used module in the batch (82 links, 43 files). The weak points are the trigger node's single GO binding, which names only the receptor-tyrosine-kinase route while the node's own text covers RAS/BRAF/PIK3CA and PTEN/NF1 lesions, and a residual ligand-independence claim that the module elsewhere explicitly retracts.
strengths: The therapeutic_vulnerability and adaptive_escape nodes are substantiated by primary human data (PMID:15118073) and a mechanism review, not asserted from the pathway diagram.
The description states the key conformance target and what each therapeutic node is for, so a curator can pick the right node without reading the file.

findings.quote: constitutively activating mutations in downstream transducers (KRAS/NRAS/HRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA), or inactivation of negative-feedback regulators (PTEN, NF1, the SPRY/DUSP feedback machinery)
findings.problem: The trigger node binds exactly one process, GO:0007169 cell surface receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway [INCREASED], but its own description scopes the node to four route classes, two of which are not RTK signalling at all: activating substitutions in RAS/BRAF/PIK3CA act downstream of any receptor, and PTEN or NF1 loss is loss of a brake rather than increased receptor signalling. The consequence is visible in the conformance data: 24 of the 32 links into this node are process_absent, and the conformers I opened are a BRAF fusion (Pilocytic_Astrocytoma#BRAF Fusion Oncogene Formation), a MAPK truncal driver (Anaplastic_Thyroid_Carcinoma) and CTNNB1/WNT activation (Endometrial_Endometrioid_Adenocarcinoma) - none of which could match the bound term. A node that most of its conformers cannot share a term with gives conformance nothing to check, which is the one thing the link is for.
findings.suggestion: Bind the routes the node claims, not only the receptor one: add GO:0007265 Ras protein signal transduction [INCREASED] (already used on the central node, so the term is cached) alongside GO:0007169, and consider a negative-regulation term for the brake-loss route. Alternatively narrow the node's description to receptor lesions and let transducer-level lesions conform to the central node instead - but then say so, because the description currently invites them here.
findings.verification: Read the module in full; read three conforming trigger nodes (Pilocytic_Astrocytoma:174, Anaplastic_Thyroid_Carcinoma:57, Endometrial_Endometrioid_Adenocarcinoma:316); confirmed GO:0007169 and GO:0007265 labels in cache/go/terms.csv; read the process_absent counts on the fact sheet.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Oncogenic Growth-Signal Lesion].downstream[Constitutive Mitogenic Pathway Activation].description
findings.quote: The oncogenic lesion drives ligand-independent, constitutive activation of downstream proliferative signaling cascades.
findings.problem: The module was deliberately revised to retract the blanket ligand-independence claim: the trigger node now says the EGFR kinase-domain lesions of lung adenocarcinoma are 'hyperresponsive to ligand rather than ligand-independent', and one evidence item's explanation says a blanket claim 'would overstate this route'. The edge description immediately below, the central node's description ('chronic, ligand-independent flux') and the consequence node's name (Growth-Factor-Independent Proliferation) all still assert it unconditionally. A reader taking the edge at face value reaches the conclusion the node text was rewritten to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Reword the edge and the central node to 'constitutive, largely ligand-independent' or 'chronic flux whether or not ligand is present', matching the caveat the trigger node now carries. The consequence node's name is load-bearing (15 conformer links) so leave it, but have its description note that for ligand-hyperresponsive lesions the independence is partial.
findings.verification: Re-read lines 57-137 of the module; the caveat and the three unconditional statements are all in the same file.

findings.quote: As our understanding of these details becomes increasingly sophisticated, it provides an important context for therapeutically countering the effects of pathogenic RTK mutations in cancer and other diseases.
findings.problem: The snippet is the review's closing framing sentence. It presupposes that pathogenic RTK mutations occur in cancer but asserts nothing about them, whereas the explanation says the review 'establish[es] that pathogenic receptor tyrosine kinase mutations drive cancer and are a therapeutic target'. The node is well covered by its other two items, so nothing is lost by replacing this one.
findings.suggestion: Replace with a sentence from the same review that states the mechanism, or drop the item; the PMID:15118073 pair already carries the node.
findings.verification: Quote read from the module file; judged against the explanation in the same item. Did not open references_cache/PMID_20602996.md for alternative sentences.

modules.summary: Models hallmark 2 as tumour-suppressor inactivation -> loss of cell-cycle checkpoint control -> unrestrained proliferation, with a contact-inhibition arm and a CDK4/6 vulnerability/resistance pair. The CDK4/6 pair is the best-argued content in the batch: it identifies the one point where a loss-of-function hallmark is druggable and states the RB-status condition that decides whether the node exists for a given tumour. Two structural problems sit above it. The contact-inhibition node is hung off the checkpoint node as if RB/p53 loss caused it, which is not how contact inhibition is lost; and the trigger node bundles brake-loss and activator-amplification lesions under one name and one p53-only binding - a defect the module's own CDK4/6 node names explicitly and then leaves in place.
strengths: The CDK4/6 vulnerability node states its own precondition (lesion upstream of RB, not at RB) and names retinoblastoma as the worked negative case, which is exactly the kind of thing a conformer could otherwise get wrong.
The resistance node's cell-cycle routes are enumerated from the cited review rather than generalised.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Loss of Cell-Cycle Checkpoint Control].downstream[Loss of Contact Inhibition]
findings.quote: Disabled tumor-suppressor circuits also relax density-dependent restraints on proliferation.
findings.problem: The edge asserts that loss of RB/p53 checkpoint control causes loss of contact inhibition. The contact-inhibition node itself names the mediators of that restraint - the Hippo-YAP/TAZ pathway, NF2/Merlin and LKB1-AMPK - and none of them is downstream of the RB or p53 circuits; its own evidence is a Hippo-YAP experiment (PMID:17974916), which is the lesion for a different trigger. So the module encodes two parallel tumour-suppressive restraints as one causal chain, and a reader following the arrow concludes that a TP53-mutant or RB1-null cell has thereby lost density-dependent restraint. The central node is the module's key conformance target with 17 incoming links, so the false edge sits on the path conformers are directed to.
findings.suggestion: Re-root the contact-inhibition arm as a parallel route rather than a consequence: give it its own trigger (inactivation of a Hippo-axis suppressor - NF2, LATS1/2, or LKB1) feeding 'Loss of Contact Inhibition', and keep its existing edge into 'Unrestrained Proliferation' so the two arms converge there. Hanahan and Weinberg place contact inhibition inside this hallmark, so the node belongs in the module; only its upstream edge is wrong.
findings.verification: Re-read the three node descriptions and the edge; confirmed the node's own mediator list and its Hippo-YAP evidence item. The absence of an established RB/p53 -> contact-inhibition route is my own knowledge, not looked up, hence MEDIUM.

findings.quote: RB1 loss and cyclin D amplification are listed together as routes to the same central node, and they are not interchangeable here.
findings.problem: The trigger node is named 'Tumor Suppressor Inactivation', binds only GO:0072331 signal transduction by p53 class mediator [DECREASED], and lists as its routes both suppressor losses (RB1, CDKN2A, TP53) and gain-of-function amplifications of cyclin D/CDK4-6 and MDM2/MDM4. Three things follow. The name misdescribes half the routes. The binding covers only the p53 axis, so the module's own flagship RB-axis example (biallelic RB1 loss in retinoblastoma) matches no term on the node it should enter at - 18 of 24 links into it are process_absent. And the distinction between upstream-of-RB and at-RB lesions, which the CDK4/6 node says decides whether that node exists for a tumour at all, is invisible at the point where a conformer picks its node. The quote above is the module telling the reader this, from the CDK4/6 node.
findings.suggestion: Split the trigger into an RB-axis arm and a p53-axis arm, or keep one node and bind the RB axis as well: GO:2000134 negative regulation of G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle [DECREASED] covers the brake whose loss the RB-axis routes share. Either way rename the node so an amplification is not filed as suppressor inactivation - 'Loss of an Antiproliferative Brake' would cover both.
findings.verification: Read the module in full; GO:0072331 label confirmed in cache/go/terms.csv; GO:2000134 label fetched from OLS (EBI OLS4 search, ontology=go) in this session; process_absent counts from the fact sheet.

findings.quote: Normal epithelial and mesenchymal cells cease proliferating when they reach high density (contact inhibition), a tumor-suppressive restraint mediated in part by the Hippo-YAP/TAZ pathway, NF2/Merlin, and LKB1-AMPK.
findings.problem: Three of the module's six nodes have never been conformed to, and the contact-inhibition node is the one that is neither therapeutic nor a resistance state - i.e. it is core mechanism that 32 conforming files have all declined to use, while the Hippo/YAP biology it describes is curated elsewhere in the corpus under its own pathway. With the upstream edge repaired (finding 01) this is worth re-examining rather than assumed to be an anchoring problem.
findings.suggestion: After fixing the upstream edge, check whether any Hippo-pathway or NF2-driven entry should conform here; if none does, consider whether the arm belongs in this module or in a Hippo-axis module of its own.
findings.verification: Fact-sheet conformer counts ('never conformed to' list) plus the node text. I did not grep the corpus for Hippo/NF2 entries that might conform.

conformers_read: Diffuse_Astrocytoma#Malignant Progression via CDKN2A/B Deletion (fact sheet)

modules.summary: Models hallmark 3 as an apoptosis-evasion lesion -> a BCL-2-family rheostat shifted toward survival -> impaired apoptotic execution, plus a BH3-mimetic vulnerability node and a venetoclax-resistance node. The biology is accurate and unusually well sourced: the vulnerability node's two conditions (selectivity against BCL-XL, dependence on a named guardian) and the BCL2 Gly101Val resistance route are each tied to primary results. The problem is reach rather than correctness. The module is named for the whole hallmark but its chain models only the intrinsic/BCL-2 route, so it is the least-used module in the batch (6 links from 5 files) and the conformers it does have attach at the generic consequence node by p53-axis or kinase-survival routes that never pass through its central node.
strengths: Every therapeutic claim is tied to a primary result with the right evidence_source split across the same PMID (in vivo, in vitro, human).
The resistance node records that Gly101Val is detectable months before relapse, which makes it a biomarker claim and not just a failure mode.

findings.location: pathophysiology[BCL-2 Family Rheostat Shift Toward Survival]
findings.quote: The mitochondrial (intrinsic) apoptotic program is governed by the BCL-2 family
findings.problem: The module's name and its place in the Hallmarks_of_Cancer collection claim the whole 'resisting cell death' capability, but every node from the trigger down is scoped to the BCL-2-family rheostat. A tumour that resists death by losing the extrinsic/death-receptor arm, by cFLIP or caspase-8 silencing, or through the autophagy and necrosis routes that Hanahan and Weinberg fold into this hallmark has no node to conform to, and no sibling module covers those (the directory has disabled_macroautophagy and stress_induced_autophagy, both scoped elsewhere; there is no extrinsic-apoptosis module). The usage pattern is the symptom: 4 of 6 links land on the generic consequence node, and the two I opened reach it by routes the central node does not model - Mixed_Germ_Cell_Tumor#Acquired Platinum Resistance via somatic TP53/MDM2, KIT_Mutant_Melanoma#Cell Survival and Anti-Apoptosis via PI3K-AKT. Both are correct conformances to the consequence; both skip the module's rate-limiting step, so the consistency check never fires.
findings.suggestion: Either narrow the name and description to what the chain models (a BCL-2-family/mitochondrial-priming module), leaving room for a separate extrinsic-pathway module and keeping the collection row honest about the scope; or add a second central-effector arm for the non-BCL-2 routes, as enabling_replicative_immortality did when it gave ALT its own node rather than letting ALT tumours conform to the telomerase node.
findings.verification: Read the module in full; read the two conforming nodes at Mixed_Germ_Cell_Tumor:613 and KIT_Mutant_Melanoma:435; listed kb/modules for apoptosis/death/autophagy siblings; read the Hallmarks_of_Cancer collection row for this module.

findings.quote: loss-of-function of the pro-apoptotic effectors BAX/BAK, silencing of BH3-only sensitizers
findings.problem: The trigger binds GO:0043066 negative regulation of apoptotic process [INCREASED], which reads the lesion as more active suppression of apoptosis. That is right for guardian overexpression, but losing BAX/BAK or a BH3-only sensitizer raises the apoptotic threshold by removing positive regulation, not by increasing negative regulation. The claim and the term point in opposite directions for two of the four routes listed.
findings.suggestion: Either add a positive-regulation-of-apoptosis term with modifier DECREASED to cover the effector-loss routes, or move those routes' description into the rheostat node, which is agnostic about which side of the balance moved.
findings.verification: Read the node and its binding; GO:0043066 label as written in the file. I did not fetch the GO definition, so the reading of 'negative regulation' is from the label alone.

modules.summary: Models hallmark 4 as telomere attrition -> senescence/crisis barrier -> reactivation of a telomere-maintenance mechanism -> replicative immortality, with telomerase and ALT as separate central effectors and a telomerase-target node. Giving ALT its own node instead of a label on the telomerase node is the right call and is argued from the literature, and the module says plainly that route is a predictive marker rather than a detail. Two graph defects undercut it: the therapeutic node points at the consequence it is meant to prevent, so the graph asserts that targeting telomerase causes replicative immortality; and the ALT node, which the notes tell ALT tumours to conform to, has no incoming edge, so it hangs off the chain the module describes.
strengths: The ALT node carries its own distribution, marker set and therapeutic reading from PMID:32175073 rather than inheriting the telomerase node's.
The notes name the wrong-node failure explicitly: conforming an ALT tumour to the telomerase node 'would assert a mechanism an ALT tumour does not use'.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Telomerase as a Near-Universal Target].downstream[Replicative Immortality]
findings.quote: Blocking maintenance returns the lineage to the telomere clock, so the consequence node is what the drug is trying to undo.
findings.problem: The edge runs from the therapeutic_vulnerability node to the consequence node, so in the pathograph 'Telomerase as a Near-Universal Target' is drawn as a cause of 'Replicative Immortality'. The edge description says the opposite - that blocking the target undoes the consequence - so the encoded direction contradicts its own annotation and inverts an inhibitory relation into a causal one. The three sibling hallmark modules in this batch that carry a vulnerability node all point it at their adaptive_escape node instead, which is the convention this breaks.
findings.suggestion: Delete the edge. The vulnerability node is already reached from the central node, and this module has no adaptive_escape node for it to point at; if a resistance state is wanted, add one (telomerase-independent maintenance or ALT switching under telomerase inhibition) and point the vulnerability node there, as resisting_cell_death and evading_growth_suppressors do.
findings.verification: Re-read lines 242-304 of the module and the edge annotation; compared with the vulnerability-node edges in sustaining_proliferative_signaling, evading_growth_suppressors and resisting_cell_death, all of which target an adaptive_escape node.

findings.quote: an ALT tumour should conform to "enabling_replicative_immortality#Telomere Maintenance via Recombination" instead
findings.problem: The ALT node is a second root: nothing points at it, so it is disconnected from the attrition-and-crisis chain that gives the hallmark its logic. Only the telomerase node is reached from 'Replicative Senescence and Crisis Barrier'. A conforming ALT entry - the module names ATRX/DAXX-mutant tumours, and four such links exist - therefore inherits no upstream mechanism, and the module's claim that the two routes are alternative escapes from the same barrier is stated in prose but not encoded. The graph reads as if ALT arose independently of telomere attrition.
findings.suggestion: Add an edge from 'Replicative Senescence and Crisis Barrier' to 'Telomere Maintenance via Recombination' mirroring the existing one into the telomerase node, so the barrier has the two alternative escapes the description claims.
findings.verification: Re-read all six nodes and their downstream lists; roots confirmed on the fact sheet ('roots: Progressive Telomere Attrition, Telomere Maintenance via Recombination').

findings.location: pathophysiology[Replicative Senescence and Crisis Barrier].downstream[Telomere Maintenance Reactivation]
findings.quote: Rare clones that reactivate a telomere-maintenance mechanism escape the senescence/crisis barrier.
findings.problem: The edge encodes clonal selection as causation: the senescence/crisis barrier does not induce telomerase reactivation, it kills or arrests the cells that lack it, and the edge description says as much ('rare clones that reactivate ... escape'). As drawn, the arrow says the barrier produces the reactivation. This is the pattern the review rubric names - a temporal or selective relation recorded as a causal edge - and it is load-bearing here because the target is the module's key conformance node.
findings.suggestion: Keep the edge (the chain would otherwise break) but state the relation in the edge description as selection rather than production - 'the barrier selects for rare clones that have reactivated a maintenance mechanism' - and consider whether the module's hypothesis/notes should record that this step is a population-level inference, not a cell-level cause.
findings.verification: Re-read the node pair and the edge annotation. The judgement that crisis selects rather than induces is my own, not looked up.

modules.summary: Models hallmark 5 as intratumoral hypoxia and HIF stabilization -> an angiogenic switch with VEGF-A acting on endothelial VEGFR2 -> an abnormal vasculature that sustains growth, with an evasive-resistance node. The biology is right and the resistance node is the best part: it states that anti-VEGF failure is a re-routing around a target that stays inhibited rather than target mutation, with the two modes (evasive adaptation, pre-existing indifference) taken from the cited review. Two things are off. The module is the only hallmark sibling with no therapeutic_vulnerability node, so its notes send a conforming treatment to a node named for resistance. And the central node - eight of the module's nine conformer links - has no evidence for the mechanism it asserts.
strengths: The trigger node carries both routes to HIF stabilization, hypoxic and oncogenic/VHL, each with its own quote from PMID:11191064.
The resistance node's two bound processes encode the resistant state exactly: angiogenesis INCREASED while VEGFR signalling stays DECREASED.

findings.quote: Inhibiting angiogenesis is a promising strategy for treatment of cancer and several other disorders, including age-related macular degeneration.
findings.problem: The central node asserts a specific mechanism: pro-angiogenic factors outweighing endogenous inhibitors, VEGF-A binding VEGFR2 on quiescent endothelium, and endothelial proliferation, migration and sprouting. Its two evidence items are this sentence about angiogenesis inhibition being a promising strategy, and the Hallmarks list sentence naming 'inducing angiogenesis' as a capability. Neither reaches the switch, the ligand-receptor pair or the endothelial response, so the module's key conformance target - carrying 8 of its 9 conformer links - is unsupported on its own content while the trigger node above it is properly sourced.
findings.suggestion: Add an item quoting the balance/switch mechanism or the VEGF-A-VEGFR2-endothelial-sprouting step from a source already cited in the module (PMID:11191064 covers the HIF-to-VEGF arm; PMID:15637262 covers endothelial/vascular response) or from a VEGF review, and keep the therapy sentence only if it is wanted for the druggability claim.
findings.verification: Re-read the node and both of its evidence items against the node description. I did not open references_cache/PMID_16355214.md to look for a better sentence in the same review.

findings.quote: A conforming entry's anti-angiogenic agent should also reach "tumor_angiogenesis#VEGF Pathway Blockade and Evasive Resistance"
findings.problem: Four of the five other hallmark modules in this batch separate the drug target (role therapeutic_vulnerability) from the escape from it (role adaptive_escape), and their notes send a conforming treatment to the vulnerability node. This module has only the adaptive_escape node, so it instructs conformers to point target_mechanisms at a node whose name and content are about treatment failure. The effect is that a conformer's bevacizumab or VEGFR TKI is recorded against resistance rather than against the dependence it exploits, and the node has to carry both claims - which is also why its bound processes have to run in opposite directions.
findings.suggestion: Split the node in two, following the sibling pattern: a therapeutic_vulnerability node for the VEGF dependence the drug exploits (with the transitory-benefit data), pointing at an adaptive_escape node carrying the evasive-resistance and pre-existing-indifference modes. Then redirect the notes' treatment instruction to the new vulnerability node.
findings.verification: Read all four sibling hallmark modules in this batch that carry a therapeutic_vulnerability node and compared their notes' treatment instruction and node roles with this one's.

conformers_read: Gastric_Adenocarcinoma#Angiogenic Switch and VEGF-Driven Neovascularization (fact sheet)

modules.summary: Models hallmark 6 as the invasion-metastasis cascade: EMT activation -> local invasion and intravasation -> circulatory survival and extravasation -> metastatic colonization, with a dormancy node for the disseminated cells that take neither fate. The cascade is staged correctly, the dormancy node is argued carefully (quiescence not senescence, and why adjuvant therapy misses it) and the module is heavily used (55 links from 40 files). What lets it down is evidence: the two most-used upstream nodes are supported by sentences that do not reach their claims, one of them a pure framing sentence and two of them from platelet-biology papers cited for MMP and invadopodia content they do not contain.
strengths: The dormancy node's four items all come from PMID:25118602 and each carries a distinct part of the claim - latency, the quiescence/senescence distinction, divergent residual-disease biology, and why proliferation-directed therapy misses it.
The notes tell a late-relapsing entry to conform to dormancy rather than model late recurrence as slow colonisation, and say why it is not a senescence-module target.

findings.quote: the biological programs that underlie the dissemination and metastatic outgrowth of cancer cells are beginning to come into view
findings.problem: This is the module's trigger node, with 11 conformer links, and its single evidence item is a review's framing sentence that names no program, no transcription factor and no adhesion change - it says only that such programs are coming into view. The explanation claims it 'frames the cellular programs (including EMT)', and the parenthesis is doing the work the snippet does not. Everything specific in the node (SNAIL/SLUG/ZEB1-2/TWIST, TGF-beta and Wnt induction, E-cadherin repression, partial and reversible EMT) is uncited.
findings.suggestion: Replace with a sentence that states the EMT program - the same review covers it, and PMID:22094253 already cited on the next node contains an explicit EMT definition ('a transient and reversible process that promotes cell motility, invasion, and dissemination') that would support the reversibility claim this node makes.
findings.verification: Re-read the node and its one evidence item; compared with the snippets on the adjacent node in the same file.

findings.quote: Activated platelets release secretory factors that promote growth factors, chemokines, proangiogenic regulatory proteins, proteolytic enzymes and microparticles within the microenvironment to promote tumor cell growth and invasion.
findings.problem: The node claims basement-membrane and ECM degradation by matrix metalloproteinases, migration through stroma led by invadopodia, help from tumour-associated macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts, and penetration of vessel walls. Both of its evidence items are from platelet papers: one is a BACKGROUND sentence about stromal induction of EMT (which belongs on the node above), and this one attributes proteolytic-enzyme supply to activated platelets - intravascular cells that are not the stromal source the node names, and not MMP-mediated basement-membrane breach. The node has 19 conformer links, second-most in the module, and the mechanism it is conformed to for is unsupported.
findings.suggestion: Cite an MMP/invasion source for the matrix-degradation claim and a TAM/CAF source for the stromal-assistance claim, and move the EMT-induction sentence to the trigger node where it supports the claim being made.
findings.verification: Re-read the node description and both evidence items, including each item's own explanation; checked which node each snippet would fit.

findings.quote: disseminating cells must survive loss of matrix attachment (resisting anoikis), shear stress, and immune surveillance, sometimes shielded by platelet cloaking
findings.problem: The node binds only GO:0016477 cell migration [INCREASED], the same single term as the node above it, while what distinguishes this stage is survival in circulation - anoikis resistance, shear stress, escape from NK-mediated lysis - none of which is migration. Two adjacent nodes sharing their only term also means a conformer cannot be checked against this stage specifically.
findings.suggestion: Add a term for the survival claim (an anoikis or apoptotic-process term with the appropriate direction, looked up at binding time) and keep migration for the extravasation half. I have not verified a specific CURIE for anoikis, so treat the exact term as unchecked.
findings.verification: Read the node and its binding; GO:0016477 label as written in the file and shared with the preceding node. No ontology lookup for the suggested replacement, hence the caveat in the suggestion.

conformers_read: Colon_Adenocarcinoma#Liver Tropism and Hepatic Colonization (fact sheet)
